summary: periodicity_scan.py drew its AR(1) and OU red-noise surrogates from parameters estimated once from the observed series; on short, strongly red series the lag-1 estimate is biased low and the global p-value was too small (anti-conservative), so a red-noise periodicity could be reported as significant.

observables: global.p and the verdict of periodicity_scan.py with --null ar1 or --null ou
impact.bias: no-signal AR(1) toys with 199 surrogates rejected 0.147 at alpha 0.05 and 0.253 at alpha 0.1 for n = 50, phi = 0.9, and 0.077 and 0.163 for n = 100, phi = 0.9 (binomial errors about 0.015); n = 200 and the OU null were calibrated or conservative; the white null is unaffected
impact.trigger: a red-noise null (ar1 or ou) on a short series (about 100 points or fewer) with strong autocorrelation (lag-1 about 0.7 or more)

outputs.how_to_recognize: periodicity_scan.py with --null ar1 or ou: JSON on stdout with best, band, global {p, surrogates, statistic} and null_model {kind, phi | tau, variance}; the fixed code adds global.null_fit, and null_fit once reproduces the old p

remedy: rerun periodicity_scan.py with --null ar1 or ou on a release that has the fix (the default --null-fit refit) for any result quoted against red noise; --null-fit once reproduces the old p-value for comparison
